Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of differently heat-treated binder jet printed samples from gas- and water-atomized alloy 625 powders

Composition.Note: Nominal composition values are specifications/ranges, not precise values. Provided composition from manufacturer. EDS measured composition is local surface/bulk average, not the same as bulk chemical analysis. O and C are listed separately in Table 1 as-received.

Process_Text.original: Gas atomized (GA) nickel-based alloy 625 powders were binder jet printed using an M-Flex ExOne binder jet printer, cured at 175 C, and sintered in a Lindberg tube furnace in an alumina powder bed under vacuum at 1225 C for 4 h.
Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing at 175 C -> Vacuum sintering at 1225 C / 4 h -> Furnace cooling

Stage4_Sintering.Heating_Profile: 5 C/min from room temperature to 600 C, 3.2 C/min to 1000 C, 2.8 C/min to 1225 C, hold 4 h
Stage4_Sintering.Cooling_Profile: 1 C/min to 1200 C, 3.1 C/min to 500 C, then cooling to room temperature

Equipment.Name: Microtrac S3500 tri-laser diffraction particle analyzer

Structure_Text.original: GA samples sintered at 1225 C were porous and partially connected, indicating sub-optimal sintering temperature. Two pore types were present: large pores at grain boundaries and small pores within grains.
Structure_Text.simplified: Porous, partially connected pores; large pores at grain boundaries and small pores within grains; no visible precipitation of oxides or carbides at low sintering temperature

Secondary_Phases.Note: Detected as double XRD peak at ~51.5 degrees in sintered at 1225 C sample

Grain_Size.Note: diameter; measurement method does not distinguish radius vs diameter; classified as undefined per Metals supplement

Relative_Density.Note: From text: density increased from 85.0% to 99.2% for GA samples sintered from 1225 to 1300 C

Composition.Note: Same GA powder as Item GA_1225. Composition shared per Table 1; see GA_1225 for details.

Process_Text.original: GA powder binder jet printed, cured at 175 C, sintered at 1240 C for 4 h in vacuum.
Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing 175 C -> Vacuum sintering 1240 C / 4 h -> Furnace cooling

Processing.Note: Stages 1-3 shared with GA_1225; sintering temperature differs.

Structure_Text.original: GA samples sintered at 1240 C showed decreasing porosity with increasing temperature, with pores becoming less connected.
Structure_Text.simplified: Decreasing porosity; pores becoming less connected; no visible precipitation of oxides or carbides at low sintering temperature

Composition.Note: Same GA powder as Item GA_1225.

Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing 175 C -> Vacuum sintering 1255 C / 4 h -> Furnace cooling
Process_Text.original: GA powder binder jet printed using an M-Flex ExOne printer, cured at 175 C in a JPW furnace, then sintered in a Lindberg tube furnace in an alumina powder bed under vacuum at 1255 C for 4 h.

Structure_Text.original: GA samples sintered at 1255 C showed further pore reduction and density increase compared to lower temperatures.
Structure_Text.simplified: Further pore reduction; increasing density; no visible precipitation

Composition.Note: Same GA powder as Item GA_1225.

Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing 175 C -> Vacuum sintering 1270 C / 4 h -> Furnace cooling
Process_Text.original: GA powder binder jet printed using an M-Flex ExOne printer, cured at 175 C in a JPW furnace, then sintered in a Lindberg tube furnace in an alumina powder bed under vacuum at 1270 C for 4 h.

Structure_Text.original: Sintering at >= 1270 C resulted in equiaxed grains. GA samples showed nearly all pores disappearing with some carbides and oxides forming.
Structure_Text.simplified: Equiaxed grains; nearly all pores disappeared; some carbides and oxides forming

Composition.Note: Same GA powder as Item GA_1225. See GA_1225 for Nominal, Provided, and EDS Measured composition. Oxygen and carbon content included here.

Process_Text.original: GA powder binder jet printed, cured at 175 C, sintered at 1285 C for 4 h under vacuum.
Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing 175 C -> Vacuum sintering 1285 C / 4 h -> Furnace cooling

Stage4_Sintering.Cooling_Profile: 1 C/min to 1200 C, 3.1 C/min to 500 C, then cool to RT

Equipment.Name: Microtrac S3500 tri-laser diffraction particle analyzer

Structure_Text.original: GA samples sintered at 1285 C showed decreased pore size and number, with equiaxed grains. Super solidus liquid phase sintering active since solidus temperature is 1283 C.
Structure_Text.simplified: Near-fully densified; equiaxed grains; liquid phase sintering active; small pores within grains and at grain boundaries; MC carbides at grain boundaries

Secondary_Phases.Note: Primary MC carbides at grain boundaries, complex composition including C, Cr, Mo, Nb, Ni; from liquid phase
Suggested by EDS at points with higher C and Nb besides Mo, Ni and Cr
Suggested by higher Mo concentration at grain boundary triple points
Detected by XRD; increased amount compared to lower sintering temperature
Chromium oxide detected by XRD

Grain_Size.Note: Highest density GA sample grain size; diameter undefined in original

Relative_Density.Note: From text: maximum GA sample density of 99.2% at sintering >= 1285 C

Structure_Text.original: GA sample sintered at 1300 C displayed consolidation and elemental segregation at grain boundaries due to liquid phase sintering. Average grain size 106 +/- 27 um, average pore size 2.6 +/- 0.4 um.
Structure_Text.simplified: Near-fully dense; equiaxed grains; liquid phase sintering; elemental segregation at grain boundaries

Relative_Density.Note: From text: maximum GA sample density of 99.2%

Composition.Note: Same GA powder as Item GA_1225.

Process_Text.original: GA sample sintered at 1285 C for 4 h, solution treated at 1150 C for 2 h, aged at 745 C for 20 h.
Process_Text.simplified: GA powder -> Binder jet printing -> Curing 175 C -> Vacuum sintering 1285 C / 4 h -> Solution treatment 1150 C / 2 h -> Aging 745 C / 20 h

Stage5_Solution_Treatment.Note: Solution treatment applied to highest density samples

Equipment.Name: Microtrac S3500 tri-laser diffraction particle analyzer

Structure_Text.original: Aged GA samples formed two kinds of precipitates: at grain boundaries, mainly composed of Mo, Nb and C and 2.5-4.0 um in size; within grains, mainly composed of C, Nb, Mo, Cr and Ni and 0.5-1.0 um in size. These precipitates were identified as MC and M23C6 carbides.
Structure_Text.simplified: Near-fully dense; MC and M23C6 carbide precipitates at grain boundaries (2.5-4.0 um) and within grains (0.5-1.0 um); gamma-Ni FCC matrix; delta-Ni3Nb; Cr2O3

Secondary_Phases.Note: Formed during aging; at grain boundaries composed of Mo, Nb, C; within grains composed of C, Nb, Mo, Cr, Ni
Formed during aging based on morphology and chemistry
Peak intensity increased in aged samples compared to only sintered
Chromium oxide detected by XRD
